input.quote: 3.8.4 Compliance. Each Party shall perform or cause to be performed, any and all of its Development activities, including Initial Development Activities, in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law.
input.rationale: This is a development and option/licence agreement rather than a services or software contract, so the rule maps to Harpoon's performance and quality warranties. Harpoon stands behind its work at or above the preferred position: (a) Section 3.8.4 requires all Development activities (including the Initial Development Activities Harpoon performs) to be conducted "in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law" - the industry equivalent of "professional and workmanlike" plus the compliance-with-laws warranty; (b) Section 10.3.3 obliges Harpoon to employ personnel with appropriate knowledge, expertise and experience for those activities; and (c) Section 10.2 gives an extensive Harpoon-only warranty set (IP ownership and non-infringement, in-licence compliance, accuracy and completeness of Regulatory Documentation and Know-How including materials made available after the Effective Date under 10.2.11, no untrue FDA statements, and no debarment with an express AbbVie termination right under 10.2.14). Duration comfortably exceeds the preferred 12 months: the Section 3.8.4 and 10.3 obligations run for the whole Term rather than a 90-day or 12-month conformance window. The disclaimer in Section 10.5 does not swallow the express warranties - it is mutual and opens "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so it reaches only implied warranties and is nowhere near the "AS IS" walk-away. No malicious-code warranty is needed as no software is delivered. The only sub-element short of the model language is the absence of an express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence; that mechanic is not apt for a clinical development collaboration, where the remedy is Harpoon's Section 11.2 indemnity, damages, and AbbVie's termination rights for material breach (including the notice-and-discussion process in Section 3.1.2). We note this rather than flagging it.
